item.title: Nicki Minaj Defends White People & Accuses Abdul El-Sayed Of Jealousy
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nicki Minaj accused Abdul El-Sayed of jealousy over a story about his parents days before Michigan's November 3 Senate vote.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj accused Abdul El-Sayed of turning childhood hurt against white people as Michigan voters prepared to choose their next U.S. senator.

Nicki Minaj posted her criticism on X on October 31 after Drew Pavlou circulated a clip from El-Sayed’s appearance on Hasan Minhaj Doesn’t Know. Pavlou framed the exchange as a complaint about white children having advantages.

El-Sayed was discussing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his own parents, rather than using Pavlou’s phrase about white children.

In the episode released October 28, El-Sayed imagined Hegseth as a high school benchwarmer whose parents cheered him on.

He contrasted that picture with his own account of being a starter whose parents never attended his games.

El-Sayed also described growing up as a brown child with a persistent feeling that he had not done enough. He connected that pressure to learning not to take himself too seriously.

Nicki Minaj interpreted the story differently.

“If you listen carefully it’s a misplaced anger at his own parents for not making him feel worthy that turned into raging jealousy of other children who had parents that lifted them up and poured into them. He’s projected all of that onto white people. He needs to mend his heart before thinking about running for any office. White ppl haven’t hurt him. He knows exactly who did,” she wrote.

Hasan Minhaj moved the interview toward campaign strategy after El-Sayed discussed his upbringing, a moment Nicki Minaj singled out in her response.

“Notice how he doesn’t get the satisfaction he was craving when the interviewer simply anchors himself & doesn’t validate that experience. We should all do more of this. Don’t validate anyone’s experience for the sake of temporary bonding,” she added.

In a separate post that day, Minaj also wrote about jealousy.

“Jealousy is not to be taken lightly. Whenever you identify jealousy, know that you’ve just identified a deadly threat. The bible says jealousy is as cruel as the grave.”

The posts followed Minaj’s October 25 appearance at Donald Trump’s rally at McMorran Place Arena in Port Huron, Michigan.

She urged Republican votes and led chants for Mike Rogers, El-Sayed’s Senate opponent, and gubernatorial candidate John James.

El-Sayed, a former public health official, and Rogers, a former congressman, are running for the seat of retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

The outcome could help decide which party controls the Senate for the final two years of Trump’s term.

Michigan’s general election takes place Tuesday, November 3.

item.title: Blueface Says DDG Helped Him Make $1 Million In 90 Days
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Blueface said he earned $1 million from streaming in 90 days and thanked DDG for introducing him to the business.
item.content:encoded:
Blueface said he made $1 million from streaming in 90 days. He credited DDG with helping him get started, from the introduction to the equipment.

“I made a million dollars in 90 days off streaming,” Blueface said in a clip shared on X. “Shout out to DDG for introducing me to streaming.”

The rapper’s claimed payday followed a sharp rise in his live audience over the summer.

Streams Charts, which tracks livestream viewing, counted about 5.42 million hours watched for Blueface in the third quarter of 2026. That was up from roughly 102,000 in the second quarter.

He ranked ninth on the firm’s list for total watch-time gains, adding more than 5.3 million hours. Most of that viewing came from conversation and daily-life content. The Just Chatting and IRL categories made up about 96% of his third-quarter watch time.

His work with fellow rapper and streamer DDG has also extended beyond the screen.

The two were billed together for the second leg of Blueface’s “Fresh Out of Love Tour.” Promotional material from Pop’s Concert Venue pitched the pairing around both rappers’ livestream followings, bringing their online identities into the marketing for their stage shows.

On Kick, creators can earn money from both monthly subscribers and viewers who send tips.

“You keep 95% of all revenue you receive,” the platform tells creators in its published revenue terms. A $5 monthly subscription pays the creator $4.75, with the rest covering processing fees.

The same 95% share applies to its KICKs tipping currency.

The attention has come with disruptions, too.

As AllHipHop previously reported, deputies have responded to numerous swatting incidents, including a gun report at a Santa Clarita business on October 19 while Blueface was live on Kick. Police found no man with a gun at the scene.

A sheriff’s spokesperson reported that Blueface was arrested and booked after allegedly ignoring commands.

That followed an August 23 call about a shooting at King of Crab on Bouquet Canyon Road. Deputies detained Blueface, then released him.

Sgt. Josh Nemeth told City News Service, “Deputies responded, completed an investigation and determined no crime occurred at the location.”

item.title: Elon Musk Calls Kanye West A “World Champion Troll”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Elon Musk praised Kanye West in a new X reply, years after the rapper's posts led to his suspension from the platform.
item.content:encoded:
Elon Musk gave Kanye West a warm character reference on November 1. He called him a top-tier troll years after the rapper’s posts led to his suspension from Musk’s social media platform.

“Kanye has a good heart and is a world champion troll. (Hall of famer),” Musk wrote on X.

The reply came beneath a post recalling Ye’s earlier defense of Musk.

West’s support for Musk has its own history. On October 2, 2018, he visited the College for Creative Studies in Detroit and urged students to ease up on the Tesla chief. A video credited to Erica Heathcote through Storyful showed the rapper standing on a table while addressing the room.

Musk had already written a tribute to West for TIME’s 2015 list of influential people. Rather than focus only on his music, he praised the rapper’s confidence and willingness to challenge people, describing an artist who wanted his audience to question things.

“The dude doesn’t believe in false modesty, and he shouldn’t,” Musk wrote. Later in the tribute, he added, “He’s not afraid of being judged or ridiculed in the process.”

Their public history also included a much less friendly chapter. West’s account was suspended in December 2022 after he posted an image combining a swastika with a Star of David. Musk confirmed the suspension, which followed a violation of the platform’s rules against inciting violence.

X restored West’s account on July 29, 2023. At the time, the company said his account would not earn money from its monetization program, and ads would not run beside his posts.

The debate over Ye’s antisemitic remarks extended beyond social media. In January 2026, he bought a full-page Wall Street Journal ad to apologize for his behavior and renounce his past praise of Hitler. He attributed his actions to an undiagnosed brain injury and untreated bipolar disorder.

item.title: Nas Credits Kurtis Blow For His Lauryn Hill Classic “If I Ruled The World”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Nas told Kurtis Blow why "If I Ruled the World" stayed with him and led to his hit collaboration with Lauryn Hill.
item.content:encoded:
Nas credited Kurtis Blow’s big-screen ambition with inspiring his Lauryn Hill collaboration “If I Ruled the World,” tracing the song back to Blow’s performance in “Krush Groove.”

In an a16z conversation released October 31, Nas said Blow gave him an image of the Bronx that went beyond news of burning buildings. Onscreen, he saw a Black man speaking to the whole world.

“You did rule the world. So I had to do your song over with Miss Lauryn Hill,” Nas told Blow.

The remake reached listeners on It Was Written, Nas’ second album, which Columbia released on July 2, 1996. “If I Ruled the World (Imagine That)” and “Street Dreams” were among its hit singles.

The move brought his music to a wider market after the harder underground sound of his 1994 debut, Illmatic. The album opened at No. 1 on both the Billboard 200 and Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums charts, with first-week sales above 250,000 copies.

That commercial reach came alongside a broader musical cast. The album paired Nas with Dr. Dre on “Nas Is Coming” and introduced The Firm through “Affirmative Action,” featuring AZ, Cormega and Foxy Brown.

Blow remembered receiving the remake on cassette and taking it into his new Nissan, which he had fitted with new speakers. He replayed it for about two hours before calling Sony with his verdict: “I think it is great.”

He recalled telling the label he expected double-platinum sales if it gave the record its normal promotional support.

The exchange gave a personal example of the influence the Paid In Full Foundation’s awards program was designed to recognize. Blow had been announced as one of the 2026 Hip Hop Grandmaster honorees for its October 24 gala at the Bellagio in Las Vegas.

As AllHipHop previously reported, the program combines public tributes with financial help for artists whose contributions have not always brought matching rewards.

Nas had discussed that mix of recognition and financial support with Grandmaster Caz, Steve Stoute and Ben Horowitz in an earlier a16z conversation.

The foundation said the gala’s net proceeds would support that work, helping pioneers and other creatives pursue new projects.

item.title: Diddy Gains New Prison Release Date After Fort Dix Transfer
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Diddy gets a new prison release date with questions looming over his institutional relocation.
item.content:encoded:
Diddy moved closer to leaving federal prison in Pennsylvania after his projected release date advanced more than three weeks with no publicly disclosed explanation.

Sean “Diddy” Combs is now scheduled for release Feb. 6, 2028, compared with the March 2, 2028, date reported last month. TMZ reported the change Monday, citing the Federal Bureau of Prisons. AllHipHop has subsequently verified the new date.

The adjustment moves his anticipated release forward 25 days. It follows his transfer from FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey to FCI Allenwood Low in Pennsylvania’s Fort Dix. The embattled mogul was allegedly involved in a fracas with another inmate as well as other controversies dealing with jailhouse contraband.

READ ALSO: EXCLUSIVE: Cassie Wins Dismissal From Freak-Off Worker’s $35M Lawsuit

The reason for the new date has not been established.

Earlier projected release dates included Jan. 21, Feb. 5 and Feb. 20, 2028. The newest date therefore brings his anticipated departure closer than last month’s March projection.

A projected release date also remains subject to revision as well.

The Bureau of Prisons explains on its inmate locator website that federal sentences are being reviewed and recalculated for pending time credit changes. The agency advises visitors to check periodically because listed release dates may change. That general guidance does not establish what prompted Combs’ latest adjustment.

His time at Fort Dix attracted attention following allegations about contraband phones and preferential treatment. NBC News reported that Combs paid other inmates for massages, meal preparation and chores, according to the supplied article.

Those reports provide context for the scrutiny surrounding his incarceration. They do not, by themselves, explain the new release projection or establish why prison officials moved him to Pennsylvania.

Combs is serving a 50-month federal sentence following his 2025 jury conviction on two counts of transporting people across state lines for prostitution under the Mann Act. The jury acquitted him of racketeering and sex trafficking charges.

item.title: Eminem Taps Wu-Tang Clan To Headline Lions Thanksgiving Show
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wu-Tang Clan will headline the Lions' Thanksgiving halftime show as Eminem and Paul Rosenberg return to help shape the event.
item.content:encoded:
Wu-Tang Clan will headline the Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving halftime show, putting the rap group on the holiday stage with Eminem and Paul Rosenberg behind the booking.

The Lions announced the booking Sunday for November 26 at Ford Field in Detroit. The team hosts the Chicago Bears for its 87th Thanksgiving Day Classic. CBS will air the game at 1 P.M. EST, and Antonio Cipriano will sing the national anthem.

“We often like to do things that are both exciting and unexpected. A Wu-Tang Clan Thanksgiving performance in Detroit certainly fits that description!” Rosenberg said in the team announcement.

Eminem and Rosenberg, his longtime manager and Shady Records president, are the show’s executive producers. This is the second year of their multiyear partnership with the Lions.

The pair’s job goes beyond lending their names to the event. Under the agreement announced last year, they help book the artists and shape the show’s creative direction. Jesse Collins Entertainment handles production.

“It’s an honor for us to team up with the Lions and be a part of the greatest tradition in Detroit sports,” Rosenberg said when the partnership was announced in 2025.

Last Thanksgiving, Eminem joined Jack White during the Lions’ game against the Green Bay Packers. White had opened the set before Eminem came out for “‘Till I Collapse.” The surprise appearance put the rapper in front of the Ford Field crowd as a performer, too.

Before the football date, Wu-Tang is set to be inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in Los Angeles on November 14.

The ceremony is set for the Peacock Theater at 7 P.M. Wu-Tang was selected on its first nomination. The group joins a class that includes Phil Collins, Sade, Luther Vandross, Iron Maiden and Oasis.

The ceremony will debut on ABC and Disney+ in December.

item.title: Drake Pops Up At Ye’s Houston Show, But Viral Shout-Out Wasn’t For Him
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Drake and Travis Scott pulled up to Ye's Houston concert, but a viral claim that Ye shouted out Drake was later corrected.
item.content:encoded:
Drake and Travis Scott were filmed attending Ye’s Halloween concert at Reliant Stadium in Houston on October 31, 2026, after the two rappers attended the Rockets-Thunder game earlier that night.

The pair had already made a public stop at Toyota Center for the Houston Rockets’ game against the Oklahoma City Thunder. Later, fan-shot video placed them in the crowd for Ye’s stadium set. Footage showed Drake and Scott watching from the audience.

The sighting quickly took on a different meaning online. A viral social caption claimed Ye spoke directly to Drake during the concert, creating the impression that the two had shared a public moment.

NFR Podcast later corrected the post: “CORRECTION: Ye was talking to André Troutman, we’re still so back though.”

That correction left the audience footage intact while knocking down the alleged Drake shout-out. It also undercut the fastest leap in the reaction: that Drake’s attendance confirmed a public reconciliation.

The concert had several verified guest moments. Playboi Carti joined Ye for multiple songs, and North West also performed. Carti appeared during “Carnival,” “Off the Grid,” “Evil J0rdan,” and “FE!N,” while the set ranged from older records to newer Bully material.

Reliant Stadium claimed the night broke the “U.S. stadium rap concert attendance record.” The Chronicle also reported that Holocaust Museum Houston offered free admission over the weekend as counterprogramming tied to Ye’s history of antisemitic rhetoric.

Drake’s appearance also followed Ye’s public backing of him in April 2025. As AllHipHop reported, Ye praised Drake for challenging Universal Music Group while discussing Drake’s lawsuit against the company.

“I have to show Drake love for going at the machine,” Ye said. He also declared, “I’m Team Drake 100 percent.”

item.title: Kodak Black Collapses Mid-Set In Tampa, Ends Show After Five Songs
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kodak Black's Tampa set ended after five songs as video of him dropping to the stage raised concern and left the cause unclear.
item.content:encoded:
Video from Kodak Black‘s performance at Nightmare on Channelside in Tampa shows the Florida rapper fall to the stage before making several sudden movements as people around him rush in.

The moment happened during the October 31 concert at Benchmark International Arena. In the clip, crew members and security appear to move toward Kodak as the music continues. The footage does not show what led up to the fall, and it does not establish what caused the movements that followed.

Reports described Kodak as having “collapsed” and said fans were calling for prayers. No one from Kodak Black’s camp or the venue had publicly explained what happened as of November 2.

The short set added to the questions. The rapper performed only five songs: “Versatile,” “Skrilla,” “ZEZE,” “Roll in Peace,” and “Skrt” from roughly 12:20 A.M. to 12:35 A.M. The performance ended after that.

Nightmare on Channelside was billed as a major Halloween concert with Kodak, Meek Mill and DaBaby among the advertised acts. The arena’s event page listed a 7 P.M. start, but the available set information places Kodak much later in the night.

Until Kodak or someone authorized to speak for him gives an account, the video is the only clear public evidence of the incident.

Concern around footage of Kodak is not new. In 2023, social media users reacted to clips from his “Drink Champs” appearance and questioned his well-being.

The Tampa video has sparked another wave of concern, but no verified public update explains the fall or what happened after the set ended.

item.title: Jake Paul Announces Christmas Eve Comeback, But Who Will He Fight?
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: Jake Paul scheduled a new boxing match with an unnamed challenger.
item.content:encoded:
Jake Paul will trade a year away from boxing for a Christmas Eve comeback in Dubai as he resumes his career following a shattered jaw suffered against Anthony Joshua.

Most Valuable Promotions announced that Paul will headline its Dec. 24 event in the United Arab Emirates. The matchup will be his first professional fight in Dubai, although the announcement left the identity of his opponent unanswered.

The promotion said an opponent and additional event details will be revealed in the coming weeks. For now, the draw is Paul’s return following a punishing encounter with the former two-time unified heavyweight world champion.

Paul, whose record stands at 12-2 with seven knockouts, framed the comeback as another test of his determination.

“I’ve spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I’d face. Nothing that’s happened has changed my belief in myself or what I’m working toward. I’m hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I’m returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey. Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn’t believe in limits. That’s exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback. We’ve got plenty of names on the list; let’s see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody’s getting knocked out.”

The holiday booking follows two heavily watched events involving the social media sensation turned professional boxer.

Paul’s November 2024 fight against Mike Tyson attracted 125 million viewers globally. His December 2025 event against Joshua reached 33 million viewers worldwide, the company said.

Those figures help explain the commercial ambition behind a Christmas Eve card overseas. Paul began his professional boxing career in 2020 and has since built a business around matchups that attract attention beyond the sport’s regular audience.

MVP said the Dubai event is part of a cooperation agreement involving the Dubai Sports Council and the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism.

The promotion also positioned the card as part of its international expansion. According to the announcement, MVP’s merger with the Professional Fighters League brought hundreds of boxing and mixed martial arts athletes under one promotional banner.

No fighters in the undercard were revealed at press time.

item.title: Ginuwine Teams With Son To Write His Own Story
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Ginuwine and his son are writing an autobiographical project inspired by AI videos, with a message about surviving hard times.
item.content:encoded:
Ginuwine is writing an autobiographical project with his son, after AI-generated YouTube shorts inspired the pair to tell his story themselves.

He told the Bronx Times he hopes his experiences can help people facing hard times. He plans to cover his career and his private life.

“I’m just trying to show people how you can still survive and continue on your journey to get better and do things differently,” Ginuwine said.

He was reluctant to call it his “life story” because he still has more living to do.

His account of grief goes back years. His father died in 1999 and his mother died of cancer in 2000. In an earlier interview, he described turning to drugs and alcohol while struggling with depression after those losses.

“I had one friend who intervened and begged me to get help,” he said. He recalled receiving counseling from his pastor and thinking about how his own children would feel if they lost him. He said he had felt alone in his grief and had initially resisted help.

The singer has also spoken publicly about asking for support. In September 2024, he marked two months sober in an Instagram post and urged others dealing with addiction to reach out.

“Don’t be ashamed reach out for help like I did bcz alot of times, well, most times, you need that support !!!!” he wrote.

He described the milestone as a major step, even if two months might seem brief to someone else. The post paired that personal update with a plea for others to keep trying.

Writing in his own voice has been part of his music, too. He told the Bronx Times he wrote about 90% of his catalog and discussed the lasting value of those songs as other artists sample them. He said he routinely approves those uses. He described songwriting as a way to express joy and pain, with listeners connecting because they have lived through similar feelings.

He also toured this year with Keith Sweat, Joe and Dru Hill.

Ginuwine will perform at Lehman Center for the Performing Arts in the Bronx on November 7 at 8 P.M., with Ro James as the special guest.
